usage.callShape: GET https://x402-geocoder-production.up.railway.app/geocode/reverse?lat={lat}&lng={lng} for reverse geocoding; GET https://x402-geocoder-production.up.railway.app/geocode/address?street={street}&city={city}&state={state}&zip={zip} for forward geocoding. Both GET with query params, NOT POST with JSON body.
usage.outputShape: body.match (boolean — true on success), body.fips.{state, county, tract, block} (Census FIPS codes), body.lat, body.lng (echoed coords), body.address (Census-canonical string, may be null on reverse), body.matchType (may be null even on success)
quirks: Registry surface lists method=POST /geocode/reverse but the real endpoint is GET with query params (?lat=&lng=) — sending POST/JSON will fail; use GET.
matchType field is null even when match=true (was null on the verified reverse call) — always use body.match (boolean) to determine success, never matchType.
On reverse geocode body.address came back null even with match=true; the useful payload is body.fips (state/county/tract/block).
Only geocodes US coords/addresses; non-US returns match=false.
Rate limit 60 req/min per IP (ratelimit header). Price $0.001 USDC on Base.
usage.guide: Reverse geocode: send a GET to /geocode/reverse with lat and lng as decimal query params (e.g. ?lat=38.8977&lng=-77.0365). Forward geocode: GET /geocode/address with query params street, city, state, and optional zip. Do NOT use POST/JSON despite the registry CALL line — it is a GET API. Read success from body.match (boolean); the location result is in body.fips (state, county, tract, block). matchType and address may be null even on a successful match. Payment is $0.001 USDC on Base via x402, sync response.
